To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the size distribution of Chinese city system deviated from Zipf's Law, that the deviations were reduced when the top 10 % large cities were excluded, and that the numerical deviations from Zipfs Law were enlarged by government interferences and reduced by market forces.
the Chinese urban system did not follow Zipfs law until very recently, and that the deviations from the Zipfs law were caused by government interferences.
the Chinese data do not fit Zipf's law because the government interferences have helped enlarge while market based reforms have helped reduce the numerical size deviations of individual cities.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the size distribution of cities and the evolution of urban systems in China.
the size distribution of cities and its implications for the evolution of the urban system and the agglomeration of urban residents across different cities.
the size distribution of cities and its implications for the urban system in China.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
China's urban system is far away from Zipf law.
the Chinese urban system has not followed Zipf's law and the government interferences have been a key contributing factor.
the size distribution of cities does follow Zipf's rule, but the deviations from Zipf are not random, but rather are the result of government interference and market forces.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the Chinese urban system has been evolving in a way that it is moving closer to Zipf's law and the market forces have helped to reduce the numerical deviations from the law, while government interferences have done the opposite.
the size distribution of Chinese urban population has not followed Zipf's law and that the deviations from Zipf have been changing in response to policy directions in the five year plans.
the Chinese urban system has been improving, and that the government should further reduce the role of interferences and promote the role of market forces.
The main takeaway from our work is that
urban system in China, as in most developing countries, is not yet mature.
the Chinese economy is not a market economy, as the country's central government still plays a very important role in determining the urban system, and thus the agglomeration economy, of the country.
government interventions have played an important role in shaping the urban system in China.
